title: How the fastest growing B2B companies found their first ten customers: three sourcing strategies
summary: Lenny researched 20+ hyper-growth B2B companies (Figma, Stripe, Slack, Shopify, Airtable, Salesforce and more) and found every one sourced early customers through just three routes: tapping personal networks, going where customers already gather, and press. Most combine the first two, and personal network matters most when you have to sell rather than grow bottom-up.

principles.text: Only three strategies source nearly every B2B company's first customers: personal network, finding customers where they are, and press.
principles.quote: Only three sourcing strategies account for every B2B company's very early growth (unlike the seven strategies for consumer apps). Thus, your choices are easy, yet limited.

principles.text: Do both: hit your network and go where prospects spend time. The real question is how far your network takes you before you move on.
principles.quote: almost every B2B business BOTH hits up their personal network AND heads to the places their potential customers were spending time.

principles.text: A strong personal network is a big B2B advantage, and you can build one via a connector investor or an incubator like YC.
principles.quote: It's a huge advantage to have a strong personal network in B2B, which you can also build by bringing on a connector investor or joining an incubator such as YC.

principles.text: Network matters even more when you must sell the product (not bottom-up), since early customers need a reason to trust you.
principles.quote: Tapping your personal network is even more important if you need to "sell" your product (i.e. not going bottom-up), likely because early customers need to have a reason to trust you.

principles.text: Press is rarely how B2B companies get started.
principles.quote: Getting press is rarely the way to get started

principles.text: Ask yourself who in your network could buy, where your target customers spend time, and what untold story you could pitch press.
principles.quote: Who in your network could be a potential customer? How could you quickly build a network?
